dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Amir, I have a bit of a dilemma. Can I ask your opinion?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Professor Sultanova has offered me a position as her research assistant for next semester. But it would mean I couldn't take the Advanced Phonetics module I really wanted.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: That's a genuine dilemma. What would happen if you said no to the research position?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: She might not offer it again. It's quite rare. But if I took it, I'd miss the phonetics course — and it only runs every two years.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: If I were you, I'd take the research position. Research experience is much harder to get than a single course.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: But what if I needed phonetics for my master's application?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: If that were the case, I'd talk to Sultanova about it honestly. She might be flexible. If she knew it was important for your goals, she might adjust the schedule.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I wouldn't feel comfortable asking her to change the arrangement for me.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: But if you didn't ask, you'd never know. What would you regret more — missing the phonetics or missing the research?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Honestly? Missing the research. If I had to choose, that's what I'd pick.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Then you already know the answer.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: What would you do about the phonetics, though?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: If I were in your position, I'd try to cover the key content independently. It's not ideal, but it's possible. There are good resources online.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: You're right. If I were being honest with myself, I think I already knew what to do.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: People usually do. They just need someone to say it back to them.

questions.text: "If I were you" uses "were" for all subjects. Why not "was"?
opts: In 2nd Conditional, "were" is used for all subjects (formal)
"Were" is used after "if" for hypothetical situations (subjunctive)
questions.correct: "Were" is used after "if" for hypothetical situations (subjunctive)
questions.hint: "If I were you" = standard 2nd Conditional form. Both "were" and "was" are used, but "were" is more formal/correct. ✅
